page.layout: One page of running text in one column. A margin note sits in the left margin beside the last paragraph. The running head is at the top centre. No page number is printed. The word "Russiæ" at the bottom right is a catchword.

main_text.p: nem ut μιμαλλόνες dicerentur decreto jussit, Polyænus Strategematum libro 4. Κλω-δόνες bacchæ Dionysii apud Macedones, Mimallones postea ab imitatione dictæ, Varinus. Videntur Clodones dictæ quasi cladones, à quatiendo, quòd thyrsos veluti hastas concuterent. Macedones mediterranei Illyricè loquuntur.
¶ MARSIGNI & Burii, qui terga Marcomanorum Quadorumque claudunt (idest retro Slesiam & Moraviam habitant) sermone cultuq; Suevos referunt. Corn. Tacit.
¶ MEDI & MESOPOTAMIAE incolæ Apostolos Domini Hierosolymis suâ linguâ loquentes in Pentecoste mirantur. Medica-rē spaca vocant, ut scribit Herodotus: quod nomen ad Illyricum pos vel pas accedit.
¶ MONAE insulæ sub ditione Anglorum linguam ab aliis prorsus differre audio.

¶ Moscovitarum lingua confusa linguæ externæMOSCOVITAE vel Moschi, Sclavoniâ lingua utuntur, licet externis linguis sic fit confusa, ut Sclavus & Moscovita se invi-cem non intelligant, Munsterus. Moscovia

page.notes: The margin note in the left margin is set in small type over three or four short lines with printed hyphens; I read it as one phrase. The Greek words μιμαλλόνες and Κλωδόνες are copied as printed, with the hyphen at the line end of Κλω-δόνες. "Medica-rē spaca" is printed with a hyphen at the line end and reads as shown; the word "spaca" is not certain. The text is in a Latin printed book with ¶ marks before most paragraphs, which are kept as printed.
